title: Finite etale scheme descent data for a covering family and canonical pullback equations
statement: Let $T$ and $U_i$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $f_i:U_i\to T$ a family indexed in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. In the category of family scheme descent data [def-trf-scheme-cover-descent-datum], define $\mathsf{FEtDesc}(f)$ to be the full subcategory on data whose local structure maps $X_i\to U_i$ are finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Its morphisms are all compatible local maps, with no invertibility condition. Recover each local scheme map from its local sheaf map by evaluating on the universal point under the specified representing bijection. For a functor $F:\mathsf{FEt}(T)\to\mathsf{FEtDesc}(f)$, with $\mathsf{FEt}(T)$ and all its morphisms as in [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], and maps $q_{P,i}:X_{P,i}\to P$, define canonical pullback compatibility to mean: each square $(q_{P,i},X_{P,i}\to U_i,P\to T,f_i)$ is Cartesian [def-pc-fibre-product]; the overlap transition on every test point preserves its composite with $q_{P,i}$ to $P$; and for every $T$-morphism $g:P\to Q$ the local scheme map of $F(g)$ satisfies $F(g)_i;q_{Q,i}=q_{P,i};g$. This definition requires no covering hypothesis.

from.place: det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images, proof (3), alteration reduction through ILO X Lemma 2.2: dimension induction in the marked plurinodal input; one relative curve, de Jong Theorem 2.4, Lemmas 5.5 and 5.7, before induction on its base; replacement prerequisite: de Jong Lemma 3.7, printed p.608, including the prime-to-characteristic level-structure choice which makes the base alteration generically etale; §3.6 supplies the smooth genus-at-least-two input. This is stable pointed-curve extension, not stable modification of a specified target pair. Moduli prerequisite: projective compactification with prime-to-characteristic level structure and its universal stable family, used before taking the closure of a generic lift. Scheme representability of the stable abelian-level normalization. Supporting input: finite normalization and its etale/formal charts. Prerequisite: An effective formal quotient atlas is a completed etale scheme chart. Comparison of the effective formal chart with a completed etale chart: the quotient atlas over each finite thickening is the finite constant-group torsor of its test object. Supporting fact: effective fppf descent for finite etale schemes, applied to the trivializations of the torsor. Definition of the family finite etale descent category and equations identifying canonical pullback.
